Command 5 printed the scene search result, then the local audit helper failed when attempting to hash a nonexistent Python bytecode cache path. Its process exit code was 1. Python used -B, so no bytecode cache was written. The helper was corrected and the search was repeated in command 6.

Successful script-internal read traces are in lookup-6-internal-inputs.json, lookup-7-internal-inputs.json, and lookup-9-internal-inputs.json. Command 5 did not successfully save its trace; no independent per-command trace is claimed for it.
The catalog was parsed internally by library_tool.py. Only filtered search results were presented to the assistant; this is not a direct full reading of catalog.json.

Command 7 showed the complete selected arvin-scene-17 card including its source excerpt. Its underlying file access is classified as script_internal_read, with the displayed contents fully read by the assistant.
library_tool.py and library_items.py were executed/imported, not directly read as source by the assistant. The audit trace records those file opens and their SHA-256 values.
claw-control was seen only as a filtered candidate in command 9; its card was not opened or used.
No direct fragment reads or distinct hash-only inputs occurred. Hashes were computed for the inputs already read.
